root_cause.text: In the Intel VT-d PASID management code, active 512-bit PASID table entries were replaced in place with a single C structure assignment while the Present bit remained set, even though hardware reads the entry in smaller 128-bit chunks, allowing torn reads of partially old and partially new state.
root_cause.evidence: The removed `intel_pasid_replace_*()` helpers in `drivers/iommu/intel/pasid.c` build `struct pasid_entry new_pte` and then do `*pte = new_pte` on a present entry, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that PASID entries are 512 bits and may be fetched by hardware in multiple 128-bit chunks, so replacement must use a clear-then-update flow with invalidation instead.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix first-level PASID reconfiguration by tearing down any existing entry before performing a fresh setup instead of using the replace path.
intent_record.what: The conditional logic in __domain_setup_first_level() was changed from branching between intel_pasid_setup_first_level() when old is NULL and intel_pasid_replace_first_level() when old is non-NULL, to instead calling intel_pasid_tear_down_entry(iommu, dev, pasid, false) when old is non-NULL and then unconditionally returning intel_pasid_setup_first_level(iommu, dev, fsptptr, pasid, did, flags).
intent_record.how: At runtime, first-level PASID setup no longer uses the replace path for an existing domain. If an old mapping exists, it is explicitly torn down first and then a fresh first-level setup is performed. This changes replacement behavior into tear-down-plus-recreate behavior, which avoids relying on the replace helper and ensures stale existing PASID entries are removed before reinstallation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix PASID domain switching by tearing down any existing entry before re-establishing second-level or passthrough mappings instead of using replace helpers.
intent_record.what: In both domain_setup_second_level() and domain_setup_passthrough(), the conditional logic was changed from branching between setup on !old and replace on old to instead optionally calling intel_pasid_tear_down_entry(iommu, dev, pasid, false) when old is present, followed unconditionally by intel_pasid_setup_second_level(...) or intel_pasid_setup_pass_through(...). The calls to intel_pasid_replace_second_level() and intel_pasid_replace_pass_through(), along with use of iommu_domain_did(old, iommu), were removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when an existing old domain is present, the code now explicitly tears down the existing PASID entry before creating the new one, instead of using a replace operation. When no old domain exists, behavior remains a straight setup. This changes replacement semantics to tear-down-plus-setup, which can avoid incorrect reuse of prior domain state or replace-path issues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix nested PASID reconfiguration by tearing down any existing entry and recreating it instead of using the replace path.
intent_record.what: The function domain_setup_nested() was changed to remove the conditional split between intel_pasid_setup_nested() when old is NULL and intel_pasid_replace_nested() when old is non-NULL. It now checks whether old is non-NULL, calls intel_pasid_tear_down_entry(iommu, dev, pasid, false) in that case, and then unconditionally returns intel_pasid_setup_nested(iommu, dev, pasid, domain).
intent_record.how: At runtime, updating an existing nested PASID entry no longer uses the replace path with the old domain ID. Instead, any existing entry is explicitly torn down first and then recreated through the normal nested setup path. This changes replacement behavior into teardown-plus-setup, which can avoid incorrect state carried through the replace operation and ensures reinitialization of the PASID entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the dedicated helper for replacing first-level PASID entries and its associated update-and-flush path.
intent_record.what: The function intel_pasid_replace_first_level(), including its full definition and implementation, was removed from the file. The deleted code validated first-level translation and 5-level paging support, configured a new PASID entry, locked the IOMMU, fetched and validated the PASID entry, warned on old domain ID mismatch, replaced the entry, unlocked, flushed the PASID context, drained the PASID PRQ, and returned status codes.
intent_record.how: This change removes the ability for this compilation unit to provide runtime replacement of an existing first-level PASID entry through intel_pasid_replace_first_level(). As a result, callers can no longer use this path to update a first-level PASID mapping, perform the associated hardware flush, and drain pending page requests via this function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the dedicated second-level PASID replacement helper, consolidating or retiring that update path.
intent_record.what: The entire function `intel_pasid_replace_second_level()` was removed, including its checks for second-level translation support, PASID entry lookup and validation, replacement of the PASID entry with a newly configured second-level entry, and the subsequent PASID flush and PRQ drain.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates a dedicated code path for replacing an existing second-level PASID mapping at runtime, so this function can no longer be called to update a PASID entry from an old domain ID to a new one while performing the associated validation and hardware synchronization steps.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the helper that replaced an existing PASID entry with a pass-through mapping and performed the associated flush and drain operations.
intent_record.what: The function `intel_pasid_replace_pass_through()` was entirely removed, including its declaration, local variables, PASID entry lookup and validation logic, replacement of the PASID entry with a new pass-through entry, and the subsequent PASID flush and PRQ drain calls.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates a code path that updated an existing PASID entry to a default pass-through mapping at runtime. As a result, callers can no longer use this helper to replace a present PASID entry, preventing that specific replacement, flush, and drain sequence from occurring through this function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the helper that performed in-place replacement of nested PASID entries, likely consolidating or retiring that update path.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the entire function `intel_pasid_replace_nested()` from the source file, including its validation of stage-1 address width and hardware capabilities, PASID entry lookup and presence checks, replacement of the PASID entry with a newly configured nested entry, and the subsequent PASID flush and PRQ drain operations.
intent_record.how: This eliminates a code path that updated an existing nested PASID mapping in place for a device. After this change, the runtime no longer provides this helper to validate, overwrite, and flush a nested PASID entry through this function, implying that replacement is no longer supported here or has been moved to another mechanism.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused or no-longer-exported PASID replacement function declarations to narrow the interface without changing runtime behavior.
intent_record.what: The change deletes four function declarations from the header/interface section: intel_pasid_replace_first_level(), intel_pasid_replace_second_level(), intel_pasid_replace_pass_through(), and intel_pasid_replace_nested(), while leaving the surrounding PASID setup and teardown declarations unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this hunk does not directly change execution behavior; it removes external declarations for the PASID replacement APIs, which restricts or eliminates their visible interface to other compilation units and suggests they are no longer intended to be called from outside their defining source.

relevance_review.reason: The changes stop in-place replacement of active PASID entries and instead remove and recreate mappings, which directly addresses the torn-read root cause caused by replacing a present 512-bit entry while hardware may read it in smaller chunks.

This group removes the dedicated helpers that performed those in-place PASID entry replacements (including first-level, pass-through, and nested cases), so its core intent directly targets the vulnerable update mechanism.

The root cause is unsafe in-place replacement of active 512-bit PASID entries while Present remains set, causing possible torn hardware reads. This group only removes obsolete helper/function declarations and narrows the interface without changing PASID entry update behavior at runtime.

This nested replace helper uses the same unsafe in-place assignment of an active PASID entry, which is the precise torn-read hazard described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the full replacement logic in the newly added helper functions. The root cause is replacing an already-present 512-bit PASID entry in place with a single structure assignment while the Present bit remains set. That exact construct is present multiple times here: in `intel_pasid_replace_first_level()`, `intel_pasid_replace_second_level()`, `intel_pasid_replace_pass_through()`, and `intel_pasid_replace_nested()`, each function first verifies the entry is present with `if (!pasid_pte_is_present(pte))` and then performs `*pte = new_pte;`. This means an active present entry is overwritten in place. There is no step to clear the Present bit first, no temporary non-present state, and no phased 128-bit-safe update. The subsequent `intel_pasid_flush_present(...)` happens only after the assignment, so it does not prevent hardware from observing a torn intermediate value during the write. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet included.
